chain_name.description:
Creates the new snapshot in the snapshot chain labeled with the
specified name. The chain name must be 1-63 characters long and
comply with RFC1035. This is an uncommon option only for advanced
service owners who needs to create separate snapshot chains, for
example, for chargeback tracking.  When you describe your snapshot
resource, this field is visible only if it has a non-empty value.
chain_name.rationale: labels which snapshot chain this belongs to, used for chargeback tracking

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls the behavior when the snapshot is destroyed, impacting data retention and compliance

description.description: An optional description of this resource.

labels.description:
Labels to apply to this Snapshot.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are used for organizing organization and management, and dont have any security impact

name.description:
Name of the resource; provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project ID is used to determine which GCP project the snapshot belongs to.

snapshot_type.description: Indicates the type of the snapshot. Possible values: ["ARCHIVE", "STANDARD"]
snapshot_type.rationale: Determines the type of the snapshot, either ARCHIVE or STANDARD

source_disk.description: A reference to the disk used to create this snapshot.

source_instant_snapshot.description: A reference to the instant snapshot used to create this snapshot.
source_instant_snapshot.rationale: A reference to the instant snapshot

storage_locations.description: Cloud Storage bucket storage location of the snapshot (regional or multi-regional).
storage_locations.rationale: Specifies the location where the snapshot will be stored in Cloud Storage

zone.description: A reference to the zone where the disk is hosted.
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

snapshot_encryption_key.description:
Encrypts the snapshot using a customer-supplied encryption key.

After you encrypt a snapshot using a customer-supplied key, you must
provide the same key if you use the snapshot later. For example, you
must provide the encryption key when you create a disk from the
encrypted snapshot in a future request.

Customer-supplied encryption keys do not protect access to metadata of
the snapshot.

If you do not provide an encryption key when creating the snapshot,
then the snapshot will be encrypted using an automatically generated
key and you do not need to provide a key to use the snapshot later.

snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_self_lin.description: The name of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud KMS.
snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_self_lin.rationale: Points to the KMS key encrypting the snapshot, which is critical for data security and access control

snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_service_.description:
The service account used for the encryption request for the given KMS key.
If absent, the Compute Engine Service Agent service account is used.
snapshot_encryption_key.kms_key_service_.rationale: Controls which service account performs the encryption operation, affecting the access chain to the key

snapshot_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
snapshot_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: This is encryption key material. Directly controls confidentiality of the snapshot

snapshot_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_ke.description:
Specifies an encryption key stored in Google Cloud KMS, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
snapshot_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_ke.rationale: An another encrypted form of the customer-supplied key.

source_disk_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source snapshot. Required
if the source snapshot is protected by a customer-supplied encryption
key.

source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_self_.description: The name of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud KMS.
source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_self_.rationale: Points to the KMS key used to decrypt the source disk before creating the snapshot

source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_servi.description:
The service account used for the encryption request for the given KMS key.
If absent, the Compute Engine Service Agent service account is used.
source_disk_encryption_key.kms_key_servi.rationale: Controls which service account performs the decryption operation, affecting the access chain to the key

source_disk_encryption_key.raw_key.description:
Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_disk_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: Passing raw encryption keys in plaintext Terraform configuration is a critical security vulnerability. A platform policy should unconditionally block this argument from being populated

source_disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted.description:
Specifies an encryption key stored in Google Cloud KMS, encoded in
RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource.
source_disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted.rationale: An encrypted form of the customer-supplied key for the source disk
